content.thinking:
I'm tracing the root cause chain: account page errors stemmed from a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py, which traces back to the monthly-spend feature flag being enabled at 22:09.

I'm ruling out alternative causes—no deploys occurred around the incident window, and the flag provider history shows only this single change. The evidence confirms the flag toggle as the trigger: the system was healthy before 22:09 with the flag off, and turning it back off restored normal behavior, so I'm confident this is the correct root cause.

Now tracing why the monthly path triggered the error: the spend calculation divides by the count of purchases made this month, which is zero for shoppers who bought previously but not within the current month. This mechanism explains the ZeroDivisionError seen at line 47 in the logs, so I've reached a valid root cause with the causal chain fully established.

Let me structure the causal chain clearly: first, account pages failed for a share of shoppers, with error rates climbing from baseline up to a peak (Gbac1, G5309). Second, those failing requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 starting at 22:09. Third, that code path was reached because the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on by an admin at P1.1, with flag evaluations returning "on" (G971b, Gce95). Fourth, the monthly computation divides by the count of this-month purchases, which is zero for shoppers who bought previously but not this month.

I'm ruling out other causes: no deploys landed before onset per T9, the running revision stayed healthy before and after per T10/T21/Gad41, and the flag provider logs show only one flag change in that hour per T15, matching the suspected cause. That narrows contributing factors down to the flag switch itself.

Looking at the rollout pattern, G971b shows partial traffic at 22:09 then Gce95 shows full evaluation coverage by 22:10 — it went to 100% almost immediately with no staged rollout or automatic guard that would halt the flag on rising errors. I'm noting this as a key gap: an automated rollback guard tied to error-rate spikes after flag changes could have limited the blast radius, and I should also check whether existing tests actually covered the monthly path for a shopper with past purchases but none in the current month.

I'm also flagging that the existing tests reportedly treat this as "the ordinary case," suggesting the monthly path wasn't exercised before the flag went live — a process gap that could be fixed by requiring flagged code paths to pass tests with the flag enabled before production rollout. Detection timing and WARN logs seem like secondary details not worth weighing as root causes, so I'm moving toward listing concrete action items, starting with running the flag-enabled test suite before enabling the monthly-spend feature in production.

Next I'm splitting the rollout fix into two separate items: one for staged rollout (releasing io-shop flag changes to a small traffic share first before widening) and one for detection (adding an automatic check that reverts the flag if account page error rate rises above baseline after a change).

I'm also considering whether PR #330's review step should explicitly include running its new tests against the current code and the fix to actually verify the zero-purchases mechanism, since the flag trigger alone doesn't confirm it — I'll fold that into the process item. And I'm noting the flag should only be re-enabled after the fix is merged.

For went_well, I should note that Argus reverted the flag shortly after the alert was raised, and the investigator was tied to the flag change after being called in. For went_wrong, the flag being toggled on by an admin without a staged rollout seems like a contributing factor worth flagging, along with how quickly it moved from partial to full exposure within a minute.

I'm treating the sampled ZeroDivisionError lines as the source of the rise, with the pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors as unrelated baseline noise. For the plain-language explanation, I need to avoid using "zero" directly, so I'll phrase it as shoppers having nothing bought this month meant there was nothing to divide by in the new monthly-spending calculation.

For the root cause, I'm pinning it to average_spend_per_item_this_month in spend_summary.py, which divides total spend by purchase count without guarding against a zero count—so shoppers with no purchases this month trigger a ZeroDivisionError on page load. The symptom description notes the jump in failed account page requests, citing the error rate before, during, and at peak.

I'm also tracing the timeline: admin enabled monthly-spend-feature, and flag evaluations consistently returned "on" afterward across logged batches. As a contributing factor, I'm noting the absence of any test covering a shopper with past purchases but none this month—existing test helpers treat that case as ordinary rather than edge-case.

The rollout had no staging or auto-halt mechanism, so the flag reached all evaluations within roughly a minute of activation, which I'm phrasing as "almost at once" rather than using a literal number. Now I'm laying out the action items: test gating (AI-3), staged rollout (AI-4), auto-revert (AI-5), running PR tests (AI-6), and keeping the flag off (AI-7).

action_items.item: Add a CI gate for io-shop that runs the test suite with monthly-spend-feature (and any flag due to be switched on) set to on, and blocks switching the flag on in production until that run passes.
Roll out io-shop flag changes in stages: send a small share of traffic to the new value first and hold it there before widening.
After each io-shop flag change, watch the account page error rate automatically and revert the flag if it rises above baseline.
Run the new tests in PR #330 against the current code and against the proposed fix, to check the reading that shoppers with no purchases this month trigger the division by zero.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until a fix for the monthly spend division is merged and deployed.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests ending in a server error went from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The service's own log reported account page error rates up to {Gbac1.5}, highest at {Gbac1.7}.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors first appear in the logs over {G5309.3}, starting at the onset, and none were logged before it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy as the trigger: the search for production changes in the day before the onset returned only the flag change, and no deploys came back.
Any other flag change: the flag provider's history showed a single flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before it was read.

The revision every replica runs: with that revision in place and the flag off, account pages rendered normally before the onset. After the flag was reverted and the revision left where it was, the service came back to normal.

causal_chain.step: That code was reached because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. By {G971b.1}, {G971b.3} of {G971b.4} flag evaluations came back on. Over {Gce95.4}, every logged batch of {Gce95.1} evaluations came back on, while before the onset every batch came back off.

The path the flag turns on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, divides this month's spend by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2}. This rests on Code-Fix's reading of the source. The logs confirm only the error and where it was raised.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that failed, likely because it divides by how many items the shopper bought this month, and shoppers who had bought nothing yet this month left it nothing to divide by.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the monthly spend path with the flag on for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. Per Code-Fix's reading, the existing test helper calls that shopper the ordinary case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division would have failed in a test before the flag was switched on in production, and the flag would not have been turned on with the fault in place.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for every logged evaluation almost at once. No staged rollout of the flag, and no automatic halt or revert when errors rose after the flag change, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path, and the flag would have been turned back off as soon as errors rose, before it reached everyone.

went_well: The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and the action was confirmed by {T21.1}.
The Investigator formed its single candidate, the flag change, {T13.1 - T3.1} after it was called in. That candidate was later confirmed by the revert.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request with a proposed fix and new tests {T23.1 - T22.1} after the incident was mitigated.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account pages call `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`, and nothing handles the case where that number is {F1.1}. So for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2} and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The failing division is still in the code, so if monthly-spend-feature is switched back on before a fix is in place, account pages would likely fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
